verdict.rationale: Google Authenticator's own docs show users can delete individual codes on the device and can choose to use the app without an account, which keeps codes local instead of synced to Google's cloud. Users can also change which Google Account a code is saved to. There is no documented retention policy, no control over how long cloud-synced data is kept, and no way to delete synced data server-side. Missing for 10: documented retention policy or retention controls, explicit deletion of cloud-synced codes from Google's servers, bulk or account-level data deletion, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can control data retention and deletion

citations.quote: To delete an Authenticator code on Android, swipe right on any code to show the delete option.
When you first open the app, tap Use without an account.
You can update the username for the code or change the associated Google Account where that code is saved.
